newsitem.title: CHINA: China sees Japan trade progress, but urges more.
newsitem.headline: China sees Japan trade progress, but urges more.

text.p: China said on Sunday its trade ties with Japan had made progress, but warned Tokyo to work harder to remove further obstacles to economic relations.
"Sino-Japanese economic and trade cooperation is basically sound at present but will improve only when Japan works harder to remove obstacles," the Business Weekly said.
Beijing welcomed anticipated yen loans and other economic assistance from Tokyo but opposed any linking of aid to political issues, said the newspaper, which is published by the official China Daily.
"We are opposed to some people's attempts to link the loans to political issues," the newspaper quoted Lu Kejian, an official with the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation, as saying.
Tokyo has pledged about $5.4 billion in soft loans to China over the next three years.
Japan has also given about $60 million worth of grant aid to China but suspended such aid last year to protest nuclear testing by Beijing.

Foreign analysts have said China worked hard not to offend Tokyo earlier this year in a row over a group of disputed islands in the East China Sea out of fears the issue could hold up resumption of the aid.
The newspaper hailed a textile agreement reached between the two sides last Wednesday as removing a thorn in the side of Sino-Japanese trade ties.

Under the pact concerning Chinese exports of cotton textiles to Japan, Tokyo had pledged to drop plans to conduct investigations for imposing formal quota restrictions on Chinese textile exports, it said.
But Beijing agreed to keep exports in 1999 at the average export level for the last four to five years based on Chinese customs data, the newspaper said.
China's trade with Japan was expected to surpass $60 billion in 1996 and was forecast to swell to $100 billion in 2000, the Chinese official was quoted as saying.
Sino-Japanese trade was $57.4 billion in 1995, the newspaper said.
